==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|let us||more formal}}
* {{alt|en|le'ss||eye dialect}}

===Etymology===
{{contraction|en|let us}}. Compare non-contracted {{cog|nl|[[laat]] [[ons]]}}, {{cog|de|[[lass]] [[uns]] (speaker with one other person) / [[lasst]] uns (speaker with more other persons)}} and {{cog|sv|[[låt]] [[oss]]}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{audio|en|en-us-let's.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/lɛts/}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛts|s=1}}

===Verb===
{{head|en|verb|head=let’s}}

# {{non-gloss|Used to form the [[cohortative]] of verbs, equivalent of the [[first person|first-person]] plural [[imperative]] in some other languages.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Let’s''' eat lunch sometime, shall we?}}
#: {{ux|en| I say '''let’s''' dance.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Let's''' buy a bottle of champagne if Mom comes, we’ll [[wait and see]].}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Let's''' go for a walk, shall we? -Sure, '''let’s'''.}}
# {{non-gloss|Used to form the [[hortative]] of verbs, equivalent of the [[second person|second-person]] plural [[imperative]] in some other languages, chiefly instructional}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Let’s''' make sure we don’t forget proper punctuation, '''let's''' not let those mistakes happen again.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Hey guys, let’s''' check to make sure that we proofread.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Y’all, let’s''' stop talking please, y’all are driving me up the wall!}}

====Usage notes====
Negation of ''let’s'' is ''let’s not'' in standard English.
*{{ux|en|'''Let’s not''' talk about it.}}
''Don’t'' is also used, but it is often considered non-standard.
* {{ux|en|'''Let’s don’t''' talk about it.|q=US}}
* {{ux|en|'''Don’t let’s''' talk about it.|q=British}}

Tag questions with ''let’s'' typically take ''shall we?''.
* {{ux|en|'''Let’s''' go to the beach, shall we?}}
